facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man presented in 2011 for evaluation of erythrocytosis
erythrocytosis, which had been presumed to be due to polycythemia vera for the past 13 years
A few months after presentation, the patient developed dyspnea
Oxygen saturation of 90% to 92% with clubbing
Scattered telangiectasias on the chest
Telangiectasias with classic spider angioma morphology on chest and back
Purple angiomatous papules on the lips resembling venous lakes
IgG κ monoclonal protein levels: 910 mg/dL
Erythropoietin levels: elevated
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Initial: 12.3%
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Later increased to: 40.5%
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Final measurement: 55.6%

concepts.why: The patient presents with telangiectasias on the chest, back, and lips, which are characteristic of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
The patient has a history of erythrocytosis and elevated erythropoietin levels, which are consistent with Polycythemia Vera.
The patient has elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels, which are indicative of Monoclonal Gammopathy.
The patient has significant intrapulmonary shunting, which is consistent with Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformations.
The patient presents with dyspnea and clubbing, which are indicative of Chronic Dyspnea.
The patient has elevated erythropoietin levels and intrapulmonary shunting, which can cause Erythrocytosis due to Hypoxia.
The patient presents with telangiectasias on the chest, back, and lips, which are characteristic of Telangiectasia.
The patient has elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels, which are indicative of Monoclonal Proteinemia.
